t.1.181.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Shaking their deerskins and their water-pots, the bulls among the twice-born said to him, "Fear must not be felt; we shall fight the enemies."
t.1.181.2: To those brahmins speaking thus, Arjuna said, as if laughing: "Become spectators, and stand to one side."
t.1.181.3: Scattering them by the hundreds with straight-tipped arrows, I shall hold back these enraged men, as one wards off venomous snakes with spells.
t.1.181.4: Thus speaking, the great chariot-warrior took up that bow, won as the bride-price, and stood together with his brother Bhīma, unmoving like a mountain.
t.1.181.5: Then those two, fearless, rushed upon those enraged kṣatriyas led by Karṇa, who had risen up in wrath, as two elephants charge against rival elephants.
t.1.181.6: And those kings, eager to kill, spoke harsh words: "For in battle the slaying even of a twice-born who wishes to fight is sanctioned."
t.1.181.7: Then Karṇa Vaikartana, eager for battle, went forcefully against Arjuna, as an elephant goes against a rival elephant for the sake of a cow-elephant.
t.1.181.8: Śalya, the mighty lord of the Madras, went against Bhīmasena, while the others, Duryodhana and the rest, having engaged with the brāhmaṇas, fought back then in battle gently and without real effort.
t.1.181.9: Then the wise Arjuna, drawing his mighty bow, struck back with three arrows at Karṇa Vaikartana as he rushed upon him.
t.1.181.10: Reeling under the force of those sharp arrows of fierce energy, Rādheya still pursues him with great effort.
t.1.181.11: Both of them, foremost among victors, could not be told apart because of their swiftness; greatly enraged, each seeking victory over the other, the two fought on.
t.1.181.12: "See the counterstroke to what was done, and see the strength of my arms!" With such heroic words the two addressed each other.
t.1.181.13: Then Vaikartana Karṇa, knowing the might of Arjuna's arms to be unequalled on earth, fought on in fury.
t.1.181.14: Then, having repelled those swift arrows loosed by Arjuna, he roared aloud, and the soldiers honored him.
t.1.181.15: I am pleased, O foremost of brahmins, with the might of your arms in battle, with this undaunted spirit of yours, and with your mastery of weapons and missiles.
t.1.181.16: Are you the science of archery incarnate, O best of brahmins, or Rāma? Or are you Harihara in person, or Viṣṇu Acyuta himself?
t.1.181.17: Surely it is to conceal yourself that, relying on the might of your arms and having put on this brahmin's guise, you now fight against me.
t.1.181.18: For no man other than the Lord of Śacī himself, or the diademed Pāṇḍava, is able to fight me when I am enraged in battle.
t.1.181.19: To him, speaking thus there, Phalguna replied: "I am not the Science of Archery, Karṇa, nor am I the mighty Rāma; I am a brāhmaṇa, the foremost of warriors, the best of all who bear weapons."
t.1.181.20: By my teacher's instruction I am well grounded in the Brahma weapon and in the weapon of Puraṃdara; today I stand in battle to conquer you, O hero, so be unwavering!
t.1.181.21: Thus addressed, Karṇa, the son of Rādhā, the great chariot-warrior, withdrew from the fight, deeming the brahmanical power then unconquerable.
t.1.181.22: But there, O king, Śalya and Vṛkodara, both mighty, closed in battle at the same moment, intoxicated with rivalry and with strength.
t.1.181.23: Challenging each other like two great elephants in rut, the two struck one another with fists and with knees; for a while the two thus dragged each other about in the fight.
t.1.181.24: Then Bhīma, the foremost of the mighty, lifted Śalya up with both arms in the fight and struck him down, and at that the brāhmaṇas laughed.
t.1.181.25: There Bhīmasena, bull among men, did a wondrous thing: the mighty one did not slay the mighty Śalya when he had fallen to the ground.
t.1.181.26: When Śalya had been thrown down by Bhīmasena and Karṇa had grown apprehensive, all the kings, filled with apprehension, surrounded Vṛkodara.
t.1.181.27: And gathered together there, they said: "Well now, let it be found out where these bulls among brāhmaṇas were born, and likewise where they dwell."
t.1.181.28: For who is able to fight Karṇa, the son of Rādhā, in battle, other than Rāma, or Droṇa, or Kṛpa, the son of Śaradvant?
t.1.181.29: Apart from Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, or Phalguna, the scorcher of foes, who else is able to stand against Duryodhana in battle?
t.1.181.31: Let a withdrawal be made from this battle, which is joined with brahmins; then, having found out about these men here, we shall fight again.
t.1.181.32: Seeing that deed of Bhīma, Kṛṣṇa, suspecting who those two sons of Kuntī were, restrained all those kings, conciliating them with the words, "She has been won according to dharma."
t.1.181.30: Likewise, who could stand against Śalya, king of the Madras and best of the mighty, except the hero Baladeva or the Pāṇḍava Vṛkodara?
t.1.181.33: Having thus withdrawn from the battle, those best of kings, skilled in warfare, all went in amazement each to his own dwelling.
t.1.181.34: "The tournament has ended with the brahmins victorious; the Pāñcāla princess has been chosen by brahmins!" Saying this, all those who had gathered there departed.
t.1.181.35: But Bhīmasena and Dhanaṃjaya, screened by the brahmins who were clad in the skins of the ruru deer, made their way from there only with difficulty.
t.1.181.36: Freed from the press of the crowd, though wounded all over by their enemies, and followed by Kṛṣṇā, those two heroes among men shone splendidly there.
t.1.181.37: Their mother imagined many kinds of destruction, since her sons had not returned and the time for alms was passing by.
t.1.181.39: "Even the counsel of the great-souled Vyāsa has turned out contrary": thus did Pṛthā, filled with love for her sons, reflect.
t.1.181.38: May the bulls among the Kurus not be slain by the Dhārtarāṣṭras once they have recognized them, or by exceedingly dreadful Rākṣasas, endowed with magic and steadfast in their enmity.
t.1.181.40: Then, late in the afternoon, Jiṣṇu entered there, surrounded by brahmins like the sun veiled by clouds, and honored by the brahmins.
